title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the Longue Marche manuscript Grothendieck lifts the modular groups to the universal-cover level, the group-theoretic counterpart of 'tangential base points' on M_{1,1}. On the previous page he showed three things. First, SL(2,R)^~ → SL(2,R) is the universal cover. Second, the preimage of U = SO(2) ≅ S^1 is R, via t ↦ exp(2iπt). Third, there is an extension GL(2,R)^{±1~} of the matrices with determinant ±1, in which elements of determinant −1 act on the kernel and on the centre by inversion.

On this page (numbered 763):
- He defines GL(2,Z)^~ as the preimage of GL(2,Z) in GL(2,R)^{±1~}. This gives a central-kernel extension (16): 1 → Z → GL(2,Z)^~ → GL(2,Z) → 1. It is not central: elements of determinant −1 act by inversion on the kernel.
- His aim is a presentation of GL(2,Z)^~ by generators and relations.
- As a first step he states (the heading 'Proposition' is crossed out) that the preimages of the finite cyclic subgroups L_ρ ≅ Z/6 and L_σ ≅ Z/4 are infinite cyclic. Here ρ is the order-6 element and σ the order-4 element of SL(2,Z), e.g. σ = [[0,−1],[1,0]].
- This follows from a corollary: every finite cyclic ζ ⊂ SL(2,R) has preimage ≅ Z in SL(2,R)^~.

Proof of the corollary. A finite subgroup of SL(2,R) is compact, so it is conjugate into the maximal compact subgroup U. A finite subgroup of U ≅ S^1 is μ_n(C). The preimage of U is R, so ζ̃ = {t ∈ R : exp(2iπnt) = 1} = (1/n)Z ≅ Z. The last step is completed on the next page.

The next page draws the consequences:
- There exist lifts ρ̃, σ̃ with ρ̃^3 = σ̃^{−2}; the set of such pairs is a Z-torsor.
- Normalised by the generator ω_0 of the preimage of {±1} (with ω_0^2 = ω_0'), one gets unique lifts with ρ̃^3 = ω_0^{−1} and σ̃^2 = ω_0.
- This is the classical identification of SL(2,Z)^~ with the braid group B_3 = ⟨a,b | a^3 = b^2⟩ (the trefoil knot group), to be extended to GL(2,Z)^~.
errors: In (16) the kernel map is written n ↦ ω_0^n. With the notation fixed on the neighbouring pages, ω_0 lifts −1 and ω_0' = ω_0^2 generates Ker(SL(2,R)^~ → SL(2,R)). The kernel of GL(2,Z)^~ → GL(2,Z) is therefore generated by ω_0', not ω_0, so this is a slip. Alternatively it is a leftover of the struck-out text, or ω_0 is momentarily used for the kernel generator.

Minor: the proposition is phrased for preimages 'dans Gl(2,Z)^~', but ρ and σ lie in SL(2,Z), so the relevant statement is in SL(2,Z)^~ ⊂ SL(2,R)^~, which is exactly what the corollary covers. This is harmless.
The reduction 'on peut supposer ζ ⊂ U' tacitly uses that finite subgroups of SL(2,R) are conjugate into SO(2), via the conjugacy of maximal compact subgroups. This is correct but not stated.

ideas.what: Z-extension GL(2,Z)^~ of GL(2,Z), obtained as preimage in the universal-cover extension of GL(2,R)^{±1}, with det −1 acting by inversion on the kernel
ideas.modern_name: extended braid group B_3 ⋊ Z/2 (preimage of GL(2,Z) in the 'universal cover' of GL(2,R)^{±}); fundamental group related to M_{1,1} with tangential base point, including complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (SL(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3 known since Artin/Seifert era); the GL version appears in Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower and SL(2,Z), B_3 informally; details unsure

ideas.what: Preimage of a finite cyclic subgroup of SL(2,R) in the universal cover is infinite cyclic, via (1/n)Z ⊂ R
ideas.modern_name: elementary covering-space computation; the elliptic elements of SL(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3

ideas.what: Plan to present GL(2,Z)^~ by generators and relations using the lifts of the elliptic subgroups of order 6 and 4
ideas.modern_name: presentation B_3 = ⟨ρ̃,σ̃ | ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2⟩ (amalgam Z *_Z Z lifting Z/6 *_{Z/2} Z/4)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Serre, Trees; Milnor, Introduction to algebraic K-theory)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard computation. The lifts of the elliptic subgroups of SL(2,Z) to the universal cover are infinite cyclic, leading to the well-known presentation of SL(2,Z)^~ ≅ B_3 and its GL extension. There is nothing beyond the established literature on B_3 and the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting.
transcription_corrections: In (16) the line under the arrows reads 'n ↦ ω_0^n' below a struck-out attempt. Given ω_0^2 = ω_0' on the adjacent pages, this is likely a slip for the kernel generator.
'on peut supposer [?]' — the image supports 'on peut supposer' (meaning up to conjugation) ζ ⊂ U.
'Proposition' at the start of the statement is crossed out in the manuscript; the insertion 'dans Gl(2,Z)^~' is written above the line and attaches to 'L'image inverse'.
